prose.text: Both maps are carried by C(σ) = Y. Contractibility is the missing hypothesis.
Allowed region C(σ)Matching colors = matching inputs
x has support {a,b}. Its image is inside C({a,b}).
Select a face, then drag x. The condition must hold for every face and every point.
A carrier assigns regions, not individual output points. For each nonempty face σ, C(σ) is a subspace of Y. Smaller faces must receive smaller allowed regions: τ ⊆ σ ⇒ C(τ) ⊆ C(σ).
A continuous map f: |Δ| → Y is carried when f(⟨σ⟩) ⊆ C(σ) for every nonempty face σ. Neither the carrier regions nor the images have to equal Y.

Every face is assigned the whole circle, so nesting holds and both the once-around map and the constant map are carried. They are not homotopic as maps into the circle: their windings are 1 and 0. Being carried by an arbitrary carrier does not guarantee a homotopy.
Source: Björner, Nerves, fibers and homotopy groups, p. 89 (Carrier Lemma).
